messages.subject: Integration in NIMBLE
parts:
Hi,

I would like to use integration with NIMBLE (as mentioned in this post https://kenkellner.com/blog/models-with-integrals.html). 

I define the function to be integrated: 
R_integrator <- nimbleFunction(
   run <- function(params = double(1)){
    a <- params[1];    b <- params[2];    c <- params[3];    d <- params[4];    x <- params[5]
    integrand <- function(u,a,b,c,d,x) {
      exp(-(b/2)*((u-a)^2))/((2*d+((x-u)^2))^(c+0.5))
    }
    int_temp <-  integrate(integrand,a = a, b = b,
                           c = c, d = d, x = x, lower = -Inf, upper = Inf)[["value"]]
    int_final <- ((2*d)^c/beta(c,0.5))*sqrt(b/(2*pi))*int_temp
    returnType(double(0)) # return type declaration
    return(int_final)
  }
)
which works as expected:
R_integrator(c(2,3,4,5,-2))

and then define the model:
mod <- nimbleCode({
   mu ~ dunif(-100,100)
  sigma ~ dunif(0,20)
   z ~ dnorm(mu, pow(sigma,-2))
 
   params_val[1] <-1
   params_val[2] <-2
   params_val[3] <-3
   params_val[4] <-4
   params_val[5] <-z
 
  L<- R_integrator(params_val[1:5])
})

However, when I try to run it it states that: 
"R function 'R_integrator' has arguments that cannot be evaluated; either the function must be a nimbleFunction or values for the following inputs must be specified as constants in the model"

Any help would be much appreciated.
Many Thanks,
Philip

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Integration in NIMBLE
parts:
Hi Philip,

The error message is a bit misleading, but at least one issue here is that the code in a nimbleFunction has to be code that the NIMBLE compiler can translate to C++.
The compiler cannot translate function() or integrate(). If you want to use an R function like integrate(), you'll need to use nimbleRcall (the link you gave illustrates this) to call out to R code from a nimbleFunction. Please see help(nimbleRcall) or the relevant section of our manual, and let us know if you have questions.

Also, at risk of raising expectations prematurely, we are planning to work to provide integration in a way that is built into NIMBLE, but that is a longer-term project we'll be working on over the next 1-3 years.

-Chris

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Integration in NIMBLE
parts:
Hi Philip,

Also, I am just realizing that the immediate cause of the error message is that you have 

run <- function

when you need

run = function

I.e., run is an argument of nimbleFunction, so it needs to be specified in the usual way that arguments are given, with '='.
As it is, your run function is actually being passed in as the first argument to nimbleFunction(), which is 'setup'.
